sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test imports
sections.what: Brings in the test tools, file reading helpers, the anchor functions, database helpers and the case and verification services used by the tests.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: AnchorService - Deterministic Canonical Serialization & Hashing
sections.title: Tests for stable hashing
sections.what: Checks that the same data gives the same text and hash regardless of key order, handles simple values, and that a one-character change gives a different hash.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tamper check fails falsely if hashing is not stable.

sections.name: AnchorService - Anchoring, Hash Chaining & Verification (part 1)
sections.title: Tests for anchoring and chaining
sections.what: Sets up a fresh database with seed cases, then checks that anchors in one case form a chain, that another case starts its own chain, and that repeating an anchor returns the same record.
sections.why: Likely reason: the chain shows the order of anchors and repeats must not create duplicates.

sections.name: AnchorService - Anchoring, Hash Chaining & Verification (part 2)
sections.title: Tests for missing results and tamper detection
sections.what: Checks that anchoring an unknown result raises the not-found error, that changing a stored result is caught as a mismatch, and that the public response has exactly the expected fields.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are the main promises of the integrity feature.
sections.watch_out: The tamper test edits the database directly, which the app itself should never do.

sections.name: AnchorService - Anchoring, Hash Chaining & Verification (part 3)
sections.title: Tests for hidden personal data
sections.what: Checks that the public verification output does not contain several named strings, such as a demo holder name, the word Aadhaar, and the names of source text and documents fields.
sections.why: Likely reason: the public page must not reveal personal data.
sections.watch_out: This only checks a few named strings, so it does not prove that all personal data is hidden.

sections.name: Anchor Database Invariant - Append-Only Enforcement (part 1)
sections.title: Tests that anchor records cannot change
sections.what: Inserts a sample anchor, then checks that updating or deleting it fails with the append-only message.
sections.why: Likely reason: the anchor log must stay a permanent record.
sections.watch_out: These tests rely on the exact wording of the database trigger message, so rewording that message breaks them.

sections.name: Anchor Database Invariant - Append-Only Enforcement (part 2)
sections.title: Test scanning source code for forbidden SQL
sections.what: Scans all non-test source files for update or delete statements against the anchor log, and fails if any are found.
sections.why: Likely reason: catches edits to the log that bypass the database rule.
sections.watch_out: The scan starts from the current working folder, so running the tests from another folder scans the wrong files, and SQL split across lines may be missed.

summary: Automated tests that check the anchor logic keeps fingerprints stable, chains anchors, detects tampering, hides personal data and blocks edits to the anchor log.
purpose: Protects the integrity logic from breaking in later changes.
why: Likely reason: the integrity feature is only useful if it is trusted to work, so it is tested closely.
how: Sets up a temporary in-memory database, loads demo cases, then runs groups of checks for hashing, anchoring, tamper detection, personal data and the append-only rule, and finally scans the source code for forbidden SQL.
inputs: The anchor service, database helpers and demo case services.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner.
risks: Some checks depend on exact error message text and on the source scan running from the project root. The personal data check only looks for a few named words.
debug: Run the tests from the project root. If the append-only tests fail, check the database trigger and its message. If the source scan fails, the message names the file that contains the forbidden SQL.
